clue.text: Maybe a stuffy sort, eccentric sir mixed in shabby clothes

definitions.note: a person who stuffs animals, with 'Maybe' marking this as a playful example

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed inside the word for shabby clothes

parts.note: tat is cheap, tawdry stuff, especially shabby clothing

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or irregular, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd, stuffy gentleman muddles about in scruffy old clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' and 'mixed' both look like anagram signals; only 'eccentric' is, and 'mixed' is fodder. 'in' puts the result inside the shabby clothes, after their second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxidermist literally stuffs dead animals, so the jokey 'stuffy sort' is a pun on that craft.

clue.text: After getting upset, eggs on wife to maintain

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word for eggs is read from the bottom up

parts.note: ova is the Latin plural for eggs

explanation.surface: Someone, once upset, urges on his wife to keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After getting upset' is the reversal signal in this down clue; 'maintain' means assert, not keep up.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a claim is to assert it firmly, which is what avowing does.

clue.text: Type of scientific old language briefly resurrected

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised up from below means the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: SCI is a common abbreviation for scientific or science

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter

parts.note: Latin is the classic old language

explanation.surface: A kind of scientific dead tongue brought back to life in short form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts LATIN to LATI; SCILATI is then 'resurrected', read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Italics are a sloping typeface, so they are a type in the printer's sense.

clue.text: Test late in the morning

parts.note: ex means former, as 'the late' can mean one who used to hold a post
AM, ante meridiem, marks morning times

explanation.surface: An assessment held toward the end of the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a formal test of knowledge.

clue.text: Two young ladies reportedly disturbed Glaswegian?

definitions.note: a Scots word, so a Glaswegian might use it to mean upset

indicators.note: the words are heard spoken rather than read, so the entry matches their sound

parts.note: a miss and a maid are both young women

explanation.surface: A pair of girls are said to have rattled someone from Glasgow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'MISS MAID' said aloud gives the entry; Chambers lists it as Scots for upset or disturbed, hence the Glaswegian.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect the word means upset or put out, matching the sense of being disturbed.

clue.text: Token gesture

definitions.meaning: a token or indication of something
a movement of the hand conveying meaning

explanation.surface: A merely symbolic act, as in a token gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign can be an outward token of something, or a signal made with the hands.

clue.text: Defect in disgrace, shrouded in a mist following corruption

indicators.note: to be shrouded in something is to be wrapped inside it
corruption means the letters are spoiled and rearranged

parts.note: a stigma is a mark of disgrace

explanation.surface: A flaw within a scandal, cloaked in fog after a bribery affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following corruption' turns A MIST into ATISM; STIGMA is 'shrouded in' it after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Astigmatism is an eye defect in which the cornea's curvature blurs vision.

clue.text: Space agency introducing cover for outermost custom zip

indicators.note: introducing means bringing something in, so letters are placed inside

parts.note: NASA is the US space agency

indicators.note: a word's cover is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: a usage is an established custom

explanation.surface: A space agency brings in insurance for the most remote customs, at no cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover for' takes the outside letters of 'outermost'; 'introducing' places them after the agency's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Not a sausage is British slang for absolutely nothing, as is zip.

clue.text: UK fuel shortages needing an alternative

indicators.note: an alternative arrangement of the letters, so they are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Britain's fuel is running short and another source is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative' rearranges SHORTAGES plus AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural gas from beneath the North Sea long supplied much of Britain's energy.

clue.text: Rest — matinee playing ET in full

indicators.note: playing about with the letters means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A rest during the afternoon showing of the film E.T.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' shuffles REST MATINEE. 'ET' misleads toward the Spielberg film.
explanation.definitionFit: ET is the abbreviation for the North American time zone, so spelt out it is the full name.

clue.text: Manipulate facts in piece contributing to wartime German article from Berlin

indicators.note: contributing to means going into, so this piece is placed within the others

parts.note: Gerry (or Jerry) was British wartime slang for a German
der is a German definite article
a man is a piece in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: Twisting the facts in an essay about a wartime German item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contributing to' sends the chess piece into the gap between the wartime nickname and the German article.
explanation.definitionFit: To gerrymander is to rig boundaries or distort facts for partisan advantage.

clue.text: Badger female about husband's display

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a female badger is called a sow

explanation.surface: Pester a woman over her husband's exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badger' reads as the verb to pester, but here it names the animal whose female is a sow.
explanation.definitionFit: A show is a public display or exhibition.

clue.text: Headland in November mist beginning to clear?

parts.note: N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the word's beginning is cleared away, so its first letter goes

parts.note: haze is a thin mist

explanation.surface: A headland shrouded in November fog that is just starting to lift.
explanation.definitionFit: The Naze is a promontory on the Essex coast; naze is also a general word for a ness or cape.

clue.text: Up-to-date short trip through Arran, say

indicators.note: one piece runs through the other, so it sits inside

parts.note: inch is a Scottish word for a small island, Arran being a Scottish isle

indicators.note: short means the word is cut, losing its last letter

parts.note: a tour is a trip

explanation.surface: A brief excursion across the Scottish island of Arran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims TOUR to TOU, which goes 'through' INCH. Arran is an island off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in touch means being well informed and current with events.

clue.text: Frequent glimpse of animal in pursuit

indicators.note: the glimpsed letter is placed inside the word for pursuit

parts.note: a hunt is a pursuit

indicators.note: a glimpse shows only a little, here the first letter

explanation.surface: Catching repeated sight of an animal during a chase.
explanation.definitionFit: Frequent as a verb means to visit often, as does haunt.

clue.text: One taking on ward perhaps wants publicity work period curtailed

parts.note: an ad is publicity
op, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: curtailed means having its tail cut, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a term is a period

explanation.surface: A guardian wants a shorter period of publicity work.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who adopts a child takes on a ward, with 'perhaps' showing ward is one example.

clue.text: Tapestry put up in disarray

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means read from the bottom upward
in shows the answer sits inside the next word

explanation.surface: A wall hanging hung up in a messy state.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit 'in' DISARRAY and are 'put up', read in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: An arras is a rich wall hanging, named after the French tapestry town.

clue.text: Weapon in destroyer briefly shelled crew

parts.note: sab is short for saboteur, a destroyer

indicators.note: shelled means its outer letters removed, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: An armament aboard a warship whose crew were bombarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyer' suggests the warship but here is a saboteur.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabre is a curved cavalry sword, a type of weapon.

clue.text: Male remains in old TV series

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A man's leftovers appear in a vintage television show.
explanation.definitionFit: M*A*S*H was a long-running US television comedy about an army field hospital.

clue.text: Out of memory on mainframe's core

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so memory follows the core letter
the core of a word is its central letter

parts.note: ROM is read-only memory

explanation.surface: Taken from computer memory stored on the mainframe's core.
explanation.walkthrough: 'core' takes the central letter of 'mainframe', and 'on' places the memory after it.
explanation.definitionFit: From and out of both express origin, as in made from or made out of.

clue.text: Off and on, barn dance welcoming unknown old soldier

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the unknown goes inside
off and on means every other letter is taken

parts.note: Z is one of the algebraic unknowns

explanation.surface: A veteran is welcomed at an occasional barn dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off and on' takes ANAC from BARN DANCE; Z goes after ANA.
explanation.definitionFit: An Anzac was a soldier in the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps of the First World War.

clue.text: Is not, colloquially, concerning English course

parts.note: ain't is informal for is not
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone casually denying a matter about an English course of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests study, but this is a racecourse, home of the Grand National near Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree is a famous racecourse, so it is an example of a course.

clue.text: Author left to be bandaged by WW1 nurse

indicators.note: being bandaged means being wrapped, so the letter is enclosed

parts.note: Edith Cavell was a British nurse executed in the First World War

explanation.surface: A writer abandoned, to be patched up by a wartime nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: L sits inside CAVELL after the CA.
explanation.definitionFit: James Clavell was the novelist who wrote Shogun and King Rat.

clue.text: Pass across start in buggy

indicators.note: buggy means faulty like code with bugs, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Move across, having just set off in a little carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buggy' looks like a pram or carriage but signals the anagram of START IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To transit a place is to pass across or through it.

clue.text: Remained dormant too long in undercover activity?

definitions.meaning: to have ... is to have overslept
a cryptic reading: sleeping in is what one does under the bedcovers

explanation.surface: A spy left too long without being activated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undercover' suggests espionage, a sleeper agent, but the covers are bedclothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Slept in means stayed in bed past the usual time, beneath the covers.

clue.text: A little wood hard to cut externally

indicators.note: externally means one piece is on the outside of the other

parts.note: to saw is to cut
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A small timber that is tough to cut from the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw is an old word for a thicket or small wood.

clue.text: Leaving hospital, popular doctor admits popular drunk

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so a piece is placed inside
the hospital abbreviation leaves the word

parts.note: Doctor Who is a hugely popular TV time traveller
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A well-liked doctor leaves hospital and takes in a popular drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: WHO 'Leaving' H gives WO, which 'admits' IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A wino is a habitual drunk, typically on cheap wine.

clue.text: Animal lifted over floor

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means read upward, reversing the word

parts.note: a yak is an ox of Tibet
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A beast hoisted above the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To kayo someone is to knock them out, flooring them.

clue.text: Duck soup made every evening for starters

indicators.note: starters are the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Duck soup is served every evening as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck soup' reads as one dish; 'Duck' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Smee is a dialect name for a duck such as the smew or pintail.

clue.text: Winter Olympics ultimately recognised following exposure?

definitions.note: a noun standing for wintry weather, the answer being its typical example

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word
exposing a word strips off its outer letters

parts.note: known means recognised

explanation.surface: The Winter Olympics finally acknowledged after media exposure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following exposure' means the synonym for recognised loses its outer letters; 'Winter' looks like part of the Olympics name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow is the weather most associated with winter, so the definition is by example.

clue.text: Range of lions missing in African republic

parts.note: a sierra is a mountain range

indicators.note: missing means the following word is taken away

parts.note: leonine means of or like lions

explanation.surface: A mountain range lacking lions in an African country.
explanation.walkthrough: LEONINE 'missing' IN leaves LEONE. Fittingly, the country's name means lion mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Sierra Leone is a republic on the West African coast.

clue.text: Recover cannabis before gangs finally start fighting

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the next

parts.note: to come to is to regain consciousness
blow is slang for cannabis

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Regaining consciousness on cannabis before gangs at last start brawling.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to blows is the idiom for starting a physical fight.
